name: Balloon Tower Blitz
summary: Stack as many balloons as possible into a freestanding tower in 60 seconds.
objective: Fine motor control under time pressure, quick decision-making.
materials: 10+ balloons per player | Table or floor space | Stopwatch
howToPlay: Give each player (or team) a pile of inflated balloons. | On 'go', players stack balloons on top of each other without any tape or support. | Freeze all hands the instant 60 seconds is up. | Count the tallest stack that is still standing unsupported.
rules: Balloons may only be stacked, not taped or tied together. | If the tower falls before time is called, players may rebuild. | The stack must be self-supporting when time runs out to count.
variation: Run it as a relay where teammates take turns adding one balloon each.
debriefQuestions: What did you change after your first tower fell? | How did pressure affect your steady-hand technique?

name: Cookie Face Challenge
summary: Move a cookie from forehead to mouth using only facial muscles.
objective: Playful laughter and lighthearted competition.
materials: 1 flat round cookie per player | Napkins
howToPlay: Players place a cookie flat on their forehead. | Using only facial muscles (no hands), they scrunch the cookie down to their mouth. | First player to eat the cookie without using their hands wins.
rules: Hands must stay behind the back or in pockets at all times. | If the cookie is dropped, the player restarts with a new cookie.

name: Junk in the Trunk
summary: Shake ping-pong balls out of a tissue box strapped to your lower back.
objective: Silly full-body movement that breaks down formality fast.
materials: Empty tissue box per player | 6 ping-pong balls per box | Elastic waist strap or belt
howToPlay: Strap an empty tissue box to each player's lower back, loaded with 6 ping-pong balls. | On 'go', players shake and wiggle to bounce all the balls out of the box. | First player to empty their box wins.
rules: Hands cannot touch the box or the balls at any point. | Players must stay within a marked area while shaking.

name: Suck It Up
summary: Use a straw and suction to relocate small objects between plates.
objective: Precision and breath control under a ticking clock.
materials: 1 straw per player | Small candies or pom-poms | 2 plates per player
howToPlay: Place 5 small objects on one plate and an empty plate beside it. | Players use suction through a straw to lift and carry each object to the empty plate. | First to move all 5 objects across wins.
rules: Objects may only be touched with the straw, never with fingers. | If an object is dropped mid-transfer, it must be picked up with the straw again.

name: M&M Straw Relay
summary: Team relay passing candy from cup to cup using only straws.
objective: Coordination and shared focus toward a common target.
materials: 1 straw per player | Small candies (M&Ms or similar) | Cups
howToPlay: Line teams up single file, each with a straw and a starting cup of candies. | Each player sucks up one candy with their straw and passes it to the next player's straw. | The last player drops candies into a finishing cup; count total transferred in 60 seconds.
rules: Candy may never touch hands once the relay begins. | Dropped candy is out of play and cannot be retried.

name: Cup Stack Pyramid
summary: Build and collapse a pyramid of plastic cups against the clock.
objective: Speed, sequencing, and hand-eye coordination.
materials: 6-10 plastic cups per player
howToPlay: Players build a pyramid from a set number of stacked cups, then flatten it back into a single stack. | Fastest completed cycle wins, or most cycles completed in 60 seconds.
rules: Only one hand may touch the cups at a time for an added-difficulty variant. | The pyramid must fully form before collapsing back down to count as one cycle.

name: Egg Roulette
summary: Take turns cracking eggs on your own head — most are hard-boiled, one isn't.
objective: Shared suspense and good-natured risk-taking.
materials: A dozen eggs (mostly hard-boiled, 1-2 raw) | Towels
howToPlay: Mix hard-boiled and raw eggs in a carton so no one knows which is which. | Players take turns picking an egg and cracking it on their own forehead. | Continue until someone gets a raw egg — they're out (or crowned the good-humoured 'loser').
rules: Only crack the egg on your own head, never someone else's. | Run outdoors or over an easy-to-clean surface.

name: Paper Plane Precision
summary: Fold and fly a paper plane through a target in the fewest attempts.
objective: Design thinking and iteration under constraints.
materials: A4 paper | A hoop or box target | Masking tape for a throw line
howToPlay: Each player folds their own paper plane. | Standing behind the line, they throw to land the plane inside the target. | Score points for each successful landing within a set number of throws.
rules: Planes may be refolded between attempts. | Stepping over the throw line voids that attempt.

name: Spoon & Egg Relay
summary: Classic balance-and-run relay carrying an egg on a spoon.
objective: Balance, focus, and team pacing.
materials: 1 spoon per team | 1 egg (or ball) per team | Course markers
howToPlay: Teams line up in relay order behind a start line. | Each runner carries the egg on a spoon around a marker and back, then hands off. | First team to complete the full relay without dropping wins.
rules: If the egg drops, the runner must stop and reset it before continuing. | No hand may touch the egg while the spoon is in play.

name: Ping-Pong Blow Race
summary: Blow a ping-pong ball across a table maze using only breath.
objective: Breath control and light-hearted competitiveness.
materials: Ping-pong balls | Straws (optional) | Table with marked lane
howToPlay: Mark a start and finish line on a table. | Players blow the ball (directly or through a straw) from start to finish. | Fastest across without the ball leaving the table wins.
rules: Hands may not touch the ball once it starts moving. | A ball that falls off the table is repositioned at the last legal point.

name: Two Truths and a Lie
summary: Share three statements about yourself — the group guesses the false one.
objective: Surface-level personal sharing to build early rapport.
materials: None
howToPlay: Each person prepares two true statements and one false one about themselves. | They share all three in any order to the group. | The group votes on which statement they believe is the lie, then the truth is revealed.
rules: Statements should be genuinely hard to distinguish — no obvious tells. | Keep it workplace-appropriate.

name: Human Bingo
summary: Mingle to find colleagues matching traits on a bingo card.
objective: Encourages people to talk to those they don't know well.
materials: Printed bingo cards with traits | Pens
howToPlay: Give each participant a bingo card with squares like 'has travelled to 3+ countries'. | Participants mingle, asking others questions to find a match for each square. | First to fill a row (or the whole card) calls 'Bingo!' and wins.
rules: A person's name can only be used once per card. | Players must actually speak to the person, not guess.

name: Speed Networking
summary: Rotate through short 1:1 conversations on prompted questions.
objective: Quickly builds a web of new connections across a large group.
materials: Timer | List of conversation prompts
howToPlay: Pair participants up and give them 2-3 minutes with a shared prompt to discuss. | Sound a timer, then rotate everyone to a new partner and a new prompt. | Repeat for 5-8 rounds.
rules: Both people should get roughly equal talking time. | Keep rotations brisk to maintain energy.

name: Desert Island
summary: Pick three items to bring to a desert island and explain why.
objective: Reveals personality and priorities in a low-stakes way.
materials: None
howToPlay: Ask each person to name the three items they'd bring to a desert island. | Each shares their list and the reasoning behind it. | Optionally have the group vote on the most creative or surprising list.
rules: No 'unlimited supply' or joke answers like 'a boat home' — keep it genuine.

name: Common Ground
summary: Small groups race to find surprising things they all have in common.
objective: Builds connection through discovering shared experiences.
materials: Paper and pen per group
howToPlay: Split into groups of 4-5. | Groups have 5 minutes to list as many things as possible that every member shares. | Obvious things (same employer) don't count — the more surprising, the better. | Groups share their best finds with the room.
rules: Every listed item must be true for every single member of the group.

name: Would You Rather Corners
summary: Physically move to a corner representing your answer to a fun dilemma.
objective: Light movement plus quick, visible self-expression.
materials: Signs for each corner (optional)
howToPlay: Label two (or four) areas of the room with different answer options. | Read out a 'would you rather' question. | Everyone walks to the corner matching their choice, then a few people share why.
rules: No standing in the middle — everyone commits to a side.

name: Zip Zap Boing
summary: A fast-paced circle game passing energy with quick verbal and physical cues.
objective: Sharpens focus and group reaction speed.
materials: None
howToPlay: Stand in a circle. 'Zip' passes an energy pulse to the left, 'zap' sends it across the circle to anyone. | 'Boing' bounces a zip back to whoever sent it. | Anyone who hesitates or uses the wrong move is gently out, or the group just keeps the rhythm going.
rules: Keep the pace brisk — hesitation is part of the fun, not a big penalty.

name: Fruit Salad
summary: Musical-chairs-style game where a called fruit triggers a mad scramble to swap seats.
objective: Fast movement and playful chaos to lift group energy.
materials: Chairs in a circle, one fewer than players
howToPlay: Seat everyone in a circle and assign each person one of 3-4 fruit names. | Call out a fruit — everyone with that name must swap seats while the caller tries to grab one. | Call 'fruit salad' to make everyone swap at once. Whoever is left standing calls next.
rules: No swapping with the seat directly beside you.

name: The Group Wave
summary: Pass a sound-and-movement 'wave' around the circle, building speed each round.
objective: Synchronises the group and injects quick fun.
materials: None
howToPlay: Stand in a circle. One person starts a simple gesture and sound (like a stand-and-shout). | Each neighbour repeats it in turn, sending it around the circle like a stadium wave. | Speed it up each lap, or run two waves in opposite directions at once.
rules: Keep the gesture simple enough that it travels fast.

name: Rock Paper Scissors Tournament
summary: A cheer-and-elimination bracket of rock-paper-scissors that ends in a crowd finale.
objective: Builds group excitement with a clear, fun competitive arc.
materials: None
howToPlay: Everyone finds a partner and plays best-of-one rock-paper-scissors. | Losers become the winner's cheerleader, following them to their next match. | Repeat until two finalists face off with the whole room cheering behind them.
rules: Once eliminated, always cheer loudly for whoever you follow.

name: Freeze Dance
summary: Dance while the music plays, freeze the instant it stops.
objective: Playful movement break that resets focus.
materials: Music player or speaker
howToPlay: Play upbeat music and encourage everyone to dance freely. | Stop the music at random — everyone must freeze mid-move. | Anyone caught still moving after the freeze sits out that round (or just laughs and rejoins next round).
rules: Freezing includes facial expressions — no cheating with a slow wobble.

name: Human Knot
summary: Untangle a knot of linked hands without letting go.
objective: Collaborative problem-solving and spatial communication.
materials: None
howToPlay: Stand in a tight circle and reach across to grab two different people's hands. | Without letting go, the group works together to untangle into a single circle or several loops. | Success is a fully untangled group still holding hands.
rules: Never let go of the hands you're holding — only your grip may rotate.
debriefQuestions: Who naturally stepped into a leadership role, and how did that happen?

name: The Marshmallow Challenge
summary: Build the tallest freestanding structure topped with a marshmallow in 18 minutes.
objective: Rapid prototyping, iteration, and role negotiation.
materials: 20 sticks of spaghetti | 1m tape | 1m string | 1 marshmallow per team
howToPlay: Give each small team the same kit of spaghetti, tape, string, and one marshmallow. | Teams have 18 minutes to build the tallest freestanding structure with the marshmallow on top. | Measure height at time's end; the structure must stand unsupported.
rules: The marshmallow must be uncut and sit on top of the structure. | No holding the structure up when time is called.
debriefQuestions: How much time did you spend planning versus building — was that the right balance?

name: Blindfolded Cup Tower
summary: One blindfolded builder stacks cups using only teammates' verbal directions.
objective: Precision verbal communication and active listening.
materials: Plastic cups | Blindfold
howToPlay: One team member is blindfolded; the rest can see but may not touch the cups. | The sighted teammates give verbal-only instructions to build a target cup structure. | Fastest or most accurate team wins.
rules: Sighted teammates may not touch the cups or the builder at any point.

name: Minefield
summary: Guide a blindfolded partner through a field of obstacles using only your voice.
objective: Builds trust and precise verbal navigation.
materials: Cones or soft obstacles | Blindfolds
howToPlay: Scatter obstacles across an open area to form a 'minefield'. | One partner is blindfolded and must cross without touching any obstacle. | The sighted partner calls directions from the sideline (no touching allowed).
rules: Guides may not physically touch or walk with their blindfolded partner. | Touching an obstacle sends the player back to the start.

name: Egg Drop Challenge
summary: Engineer a contraption that protects a raw egg dropped from height.
objective: Applies design thinking with a satisfying pass/fail test.
materials: Raw eggs | Straws, tape, paper, balloons or similar craft supplies | A drop point (stairwell or balcony)
howToPlay: Give each team an identical kit of building materials and one raw egg. | Teams build a protective contraption within a time limit. | Drop each contraption from an agreed height — surviving eggs win.
rules: The egg must be visible and not wrapped so heavily it can't be inspected before dropping.

name: The Perfect Square
summary: Blindfolded team forms a perfect square using only a length of rope.
objective: Group communication and consensus-building without sight.
materials: A long loop of rope | Blindfolds
howToPlay: Blindfold the whole team and have them hold a large loop of rope. | Without removing blindfolds, they must arrange themselves and the rope into a perfect square. | Remove blindfolds together to reveal the result.
rules: No peeking until everyone agrees the shape is finished.

name: Trust Fall
summary: Fall backward, trusting teammates to catch you.
objective: Builds visible, immediate trust between pairs or small groups.
materials: Soft, flat ground
howToPlay: One person stands with arms crossed on a raised, stable platform (or simply stands rigid). | A line of catchers stands close behind, arms out and ready. | On a clear countdown, the person falls straight back and is caught.
rules: Always brief safe hand and body positioning before starting. | Never attempt without confirmed, attentive catchers ready.

name: Blindfolded Trail
summary: Lead a blindfolded partner along a trail using only touch and spoken cues.
objective: Deepens trust and non-verbal communication between pairs.
materials: Blindfolds | An outdoor or safe indoor path
howToPlay: Pair up; one partner is blindfolded and the other guides them along a set trail. | Guides may use a light hand on the shoulder plus spoken instructions. | Swap roles halfway through the trail.
rules: Guides are fully responsible for their partner's safety at all times.

name: Back-to-Back Drawing
summary: Describe a shape or picture for your partner to draw without seeing it.
objective: Highlights how precise, patient language improves shared understanding.
materials: Paper | Pens | Simple reference images
howToPlay: Pairs sit back-to-back; one holds a reference image, the other holds blank paper. | The describer explains the image using only words (no shape names allowed for extra challenge). | The drawer sketches based purely on the description, then compare results.
rules: No peeking, and the drawer may not ask yes/no questions in the harder variant.

name: Silent Line-Up
summary: Arrange the whole group in order (like birthdays) without speaking.
objective: Forces creative non-verbal communication and patience.
materials: None
howToPlay: Pick an order criterion (birthday month, height, alphabetical first name). | Without speaking or writing, the group arranges itself into that order using gestures only. | Check the result out loud once everyone is satisfied.
rules: No talking, mouthing words, or writing — gestures and expressions only.

name: Compass Walk
summary: Guide a blindfolded partner using only four directional words.
objective: Practises concise, high-trust instruction-giving.
materials: Blindfolds | Open space with light obstacles
howToPlay: Pair up; one is blindfolded, the other may only say 'forward', 'back', 'left', or 'right'. | The guide directs their partner through a short obstacle course using just those four words. | Swap roles and compare completion times.
rules: No other words or physical contact are allowed during the walk.

name: Tug of War
summary: Classic two-team rope pull to a centre line.
objective: Full-team physical cooperation and shared effort.
materials: Thick rope | Centre-line marker
howToPlay: Split into two evenly matched teams on either end of a rope. | On 'go', both teams pull to drag the centre marker past their line. | Best of three rounds wins the match.
rules: No wrapping the rope around hands or body — grip only. | Stop immediately on the referee's whistle.

name: Amazing Race Scavenger Hunt
summary: Teams race between checkpoints completing challenges and clues.
objective: Combines navigation, problem-solving, and physical activity.
materials: Printed clue cards | Checkpoint props/challenges | Route map
howToPlay: Set up a series of checkpoints across a venue or neighbourhood, each with a clue and a mini-challenge. | Teams start staggered and race to complete each checkpoint before getting the next clue. | First team to complete all checkpoints and reach the finish wins.
rules: Teams must complete each checkpoint challenge before moving on. | No sharing clues between teams.

name: Relay Sack Race
summary: Hop in sacks along a relay course as a team.
objective: Playful physical challenge with team hand-offs.
materials: Sacks or large pillowcases | Course markers
howToPlay: Teams line up in relay order; each runner hops inside a sack to a turn-around point and back. | Hand the sack to the next teammate; first team finished wins.
rules: Both feet must stay inside the sack while hopping. | Falling requires standing back up before continuing.

name: Balloon Volleyball
summary: Keep a balloon off the ground volleyball-style over a low net or rope.
objective: Light cardio and team coordination without needing much space.
materials: Balloons | A rope or string as a net (optional)
howToPlay: Split into two teams facing each other across a rope or line. | Volley the balloon back and forth; a team scores if it touches the ground on the opponent's side. | Play to a set number of points.
rules: No catching or holding the balloon — tap it only. | Each side gets up to 3 touches before sending it over.

name: Mini Terrarium Building
summary: Layer soil, stones, and plants into a personal take-home terrarium.
objective: A calm, creative activity that produces a lasting keepsake.
materials: Glass jars | Pebbles, charcoal, soil | Small succulents or moss | Decorative figurines
howToPlay: Set up stations with layered materials: drainage stones, charcoal, soil, then plants. | Guide participants to layer their jar step by step and plant their succulent. | Finish with optional decorative touches like figurines or coloured sand.
rules: Handle glass jars carefully; keep soil and water off shared surfaces.

name: Collaborative Team Mural
summary: Each person paints one tile that combines into a single large team artwork.
objective: Symbolises individual contribution forming a shared whole.
materials: Canvas or wood panels cut into a grid | Acrylic paints | Brushes | A reference image
howToPlay: Divide a large reference image into one numbered panel per participant. | Each person paints their panel to match their section of the image. | Assemble all panels together to reveal the completed mural.
rules: Stick to the assigned panel's colours and lines so the final image lines up.

name: Virtual Scavenger Hunt
summary: Race to find household items matching a list, shown live on camera.
objective: Injects movement and fun into a remote call.
materials: Video call platform | A list of items to find
howToPlay: Read out an item (e.g., 'something red', 'a coffee mug') on the call. | Everyone dashes to grab a matching item and holds it up to camera. | Last person back or unable to find an item is out; last one standing wins.
rules: Items must genuinely be found in the current room — no pre-staging.

name: Online Pictionary Battle
summary: Teams guess a teammate's live digital drawing before time runs out.
objective: Fun creative pressure that works great over video call.
materials: Shared whiteboard tool (screen share) | A list of prompt words
howToPlay: Split into teams; one drawer per team gets a secret prompt word. | Drawers sketch on a shared digital whiteboard while their team guesses out loud. | First team to guess correctly scores a point; rotate the drawer each round.
rules: No writing letters, numbers, or speaking while drawing.
